name: Bird's Opening
summary: White controls the key central square from the side with a pawn, a knight and a long-range bishop, then castles into a safe, flexible setup.

goal.title: Take control of the key central square
goal.text: White's side pawn and a knight both watch the square in front of Black's central pawns, and the bishop soon joins them from the long diagonal. Meanwhile White tucks the king away early and keeps a solid, compact setup. From that safe base White decides when to break open the center.
plans: Use the side pawn and a knight to control the key central square (marked on the board).
Put the bishop on the long diagonal so it also eyes that square and the far corner.
Castle early and keep the pawns in front of the king solid.
Once the pieces are out, break open the center with a central pawn push, or plant a knight on the key square.

variations.name: Main line: 1...d5 (Black builds a classical center)
variations.strategy: Black grabs the center with pawns, so White does not rush. Bring out the knight, support the center with a solid pawn, put the bishop on the long diagonal, then castle. It is like a Dutch Defense with the colors reversed: keep control of the key central square and wait for the right moment to jump in with a knight or push a central pawn.

variations.name: From's Gambit: 1...e5 (Black offers a pawn)
variations.strategy: Black offers a pawn right away, so take it. After the trades White is a pawn up, but Black's pieces come out fast and a black pawn may chase your knight. Stay calm: let the knight hop to the edge of the board, put a pawn in the center and trade off Black's most dangerous knight. Once the first wave of attacks runs out, use the extra pawn and aim your rooks along the half-open file at Black's weak pawn.

variations.name: Vs 1...Nf6: a flexible kingside setup
variations.strategy: Against the knight move, White keeps the same compact plan: knight and bishop to natural squares, a solid pawn in front of the king, castle, then take the center with the central pawn push. Do not commit the queen-side pieces until you see what Black is planning.

variations.name: Main line with ...c5: Black hits the center from the side
variations.strategy: This is the main setup again, but Black strikes at the center with a side pawn. Stay calm: the bishop on the long diagonal and the knight keep an eye on the key central square, and the solid pawn structure leaves no weakness to attack. Finish development and castle before deciding how to use the center.

variations.name: Vs 1...c5: the Sicilian-style reply
variations.strategy: Against the side-pawn reply White does not need to rush. Develop the knight, free the bishop with a solid pawn, then place the other bishop on the long diagonal after a pawn move on the queen side. Castle early and decide between a central pawn push or a knight jump once Black commits.

variations.strategy: Black plans a fianchettoed bishop on the long diagonal of their own. White keeps the compact setup: knight out, solid pawn behind the king, bishop to the near side, castle, and then take the center with the central pawn.

variations.name: Vs 1...e6: Black builds a solid, closed structure
variations.strategy: Black chooses a sturdy pawn wall. White answers with the same compact setup, but this time one bishop heads to a more active square aimed at Black's king side, and the other takes the long diagonal. Keep the knight ready to jump to the key central square.

variations.name: 1...d5 2.Nf3 Nc6: Black develops fast and pins the knight
variations.strategy: Black develops quickly and pins your knight against the queen. Stay calm: unpin by developing the bishop, castle, then bring the other bishop to the long diagonal. Black's bishop will eye your f-pawn, so keep an eye on it and keep control of the key central square.

variations.name: Vs 1...f5: the Dutch-style reply
variations.strategy: Black copies your pawn move, so both sides share the same structure. Play the compact setup you know: knight out, a solid pawn behind the king, bishop to the near side, castle, then take the center with the central pawn. Remember that Black's fianchettoed bishop will look along the long diagonal.

variations.name: Vs 1...d6: a modest reply
variations.strategy: Black prepares a flexible setup with a modest pawn move. Answer with the same compact plan: knight and bishop to natural squares, castle, then take the center with the central pawn. Do not rush; there is nothing to punish yet.
